title: Retire a Cargo Tag Without Leaving a Stale View
scenario: At a harbor inspection station, a dock supervisor uses a DockConsole to adjust the priority on the active CargoTag, while an AuditDisplay shows the same tag to an inspector. Cargo tags are created for a shift and later retired, so both station devices must stop using an old tag before or when they switch to a live replacement.
problem_statement: `DockConsole::assign`, `AuditDisplay::watch`, and the two `clear` operations currently lose or retain the wrong CargoTag state. Make the console and display follow the selected live tag, ensure `DockConsole::boostPriority` changes the tag seen by `AuditDisplay`, and ensure the display can switch away from a retired tag before it is queried again.
constraints: Do not change the public methods or data members of `CargoTag`, `DockConsole`, or `AuditDisplay`.
`DockConsole` may change the priority of its active tag, while `AuditDisplay` only reports information.
A console and display may be assigned to the same live CargoTag.
A tag can be retired after the display has switched to another live tag.
The public query methods must remain safe when no tag is assigned.
learning_objective: Use raw non-owning pointer members to preserve pointee identity, represent null state, support aliasing between holders, mutate a shared heap pointee through a writable pointer, reseat a pointer before a former pointee is retired, and avoid dereferencing stale pointers.
instructions: Correct the assignment, clearing, and viewing behavior in the existing classes. Keep the null-aware query behavior intact, and do not add ownership to either station device.
expected_concepts: multiple pointer holders aliasing one pointee
dereference-based mutation through a raw pointer
hints: The console and the display should be able to refer to the same tag rather than each maintaining a separate tag state.
After the console changes a tag's priority, the display should report that changed priority without being assigned again.
When a station is cleared or switched to a replacement tag, later queries must use the new state rather than an earlier retired tag.
explanation: The station devices do not own CargoTag objects; they only remember which currently live tag they are using. Assigning the incoming tag lets the console and display refer to the same object, so a priority change made through the console is visible on the display. Clearing removes a station's current association, and switching the display to a replacement removes its association with the old tag before that old tag is retired.
learner_goal: Make the dock console and audit display stay synchronized on the same live cargo tag, support switching to a replacement tag, and avoid reporting a retired tag.
